question: Which of the following is the system designed to prevent unauthorised access to or from a private network?
solution:
The correct answer is **Firewall**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **firewall** is a network security device that monitors and filters incoming and outgoing network traffic based on an organization's previously established security policies.
 
• At its most basic, a firewall is essentially the barrier that sits between a private internal network and the public Internet.
 
• The main purpose of a firewall is to prevent unauthorised access to or from private networks and to protect the networked computer system from malicious access.
 
• Firewalls can be hardware, software, or a combination of both.
 
• Types of firewalls include packet filtering firewalls, stateful inspection firewalls, proxy firewalls, and next-generation firewalls (NGFW).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Firewalls have evolved over time to combat the increasing complexity and sophistication of cyber threats. Here are some key milestones:

 
• The concept of a firewall originally emerged in the late 1980s when the Internet was a fledgling network.
 
• One of the first types of firewalls to be developed was the packet filter firewall, which made decisions to allow or block traffic based on IP addresses and ports.
 
• As cyber threats evolved, so did firewall technology, leading to the development of stateful inspection firewalls, which could make decisions based on the context of network traffic.
 
• The introduction of next-generation firewalls (NGFW) brought features such as application awareness and control, integrated intrusion prevention, and cloud-delivered threat intelligence.
 
• Today, firewalls are an essential component of any organization's cybersecurity strategy, protecting against a wide range of cyber threats while enabling secure access to network resources
